In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CHS PPL have the ability to kill some but not all kinds of target cells, and the mechanisms involved in the killing are not limited to perforin.
CHS PPL have a defect in the perforin‐mediating cytotoxicity pathway, but that they are able to kill certain target cells via a non‐MHC class‐I restricted mechanism that is not fully understood.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perforin‐dependent cytotoxicity is impaired in CHS lymphocytes and that FasL‐mediated cytolytic activity is not impaired in CHS.
CHS PPL have an ability to exert cytotoxicity via a perforin, a Fas‐FasL, and a TNF‐α‐mediated pathway.
CHS PTL can utilize at least two cytolytic mechanisms, a perforin‐dependent pathway and a perforin‐independent pathway, to kill target cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytotoxicity mediated by CHS PBL is not restricted to a single cytotoxic molecule, and that the CHS PML is not a single cytotoxic protein.
CHS PMLs have a functional cytolytic mechanism that is not dependent on perforin or FasL.
